chunks: From him, from Abu Ja'far, from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, from his father عليه السلام, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said:
A cow and a jadha'ah suffice for three members of one household, a musinnah suffices for seven separate individuals, and a jazur suffices for ten separate individuals.

key_terms.الْبَقَرَةُ: a cow used as a sacrificial animal
key_terms.الْجَذَعَةُ: a young sacrificial animal that is legally sufficient in this context
key_terms.الْجَزُورُ: a camel slaughtered as a sacrificial animal
key_terms.تُجْزِي: suffices or fulfills the required obligation
key_terms.مُتَفَرِّقِينَ: separate individuals not belonging to one household grouping

ai.seo_question: How many people can share in a sacrificial animal at Mina according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the number of people for whom certain sacrificial animals suffice in the rites at Mina. It is a jurisprudential ruling concerning hajj sacrifice shares, distinguishing between members of one household and separate individuals.
